EIP-2771 context mixin.
 When called through the trusted KuluriForwarder, the real sender is the last
 20 bytes of calldata. Direct calls fall back to msg.sender (backend, tests).

KuluriAgreement
 A mutual job agreement between a farm and a seasonal worker.
 Deployed by KuluriAgreementFactory (a neutral platform contract).
 Power balance
 ─────────────
 Neither party can unilaterally create an active agreement.
 - The factory deploys this (no single party controls deployment).
 - The farm signs first (proposes terms).
 - The worker must independently verify the hash and sign to make it Agreed.
 - Extensions work the same way: one side proposes, the other confirms.
 - Only the factory can deploy — no one can create a fake Kuluri agreement.
 Lifecycle
 ─────────
   Proposed ──[workerAgrees]──→ Agreed ──[markCompleted]──→ Completed
            ↘[farm withdraws]→ Withdrawn  └──[cancel]──────→ Cancelled
 Extensions
 ──────────
 Either party can propose an extension while status is Agreed.
 The other party must confirm it. The extension replaces the active terms hash
 and end date. Every extension is stored permanently as an immutable record.
 What is stored on-chain
 ───────────────────────
 Only the keccak256 hash of the full terms JSON — no names, no PII (GDPR).
 The app keeps the readable text. Anyone with the original JSON can verify it.

Farm corrects the terms hash before the worker has signed.
 The new hash must differ — prevents pointless no-op calls.
Farm pulls the proposal back before the worker signs.

Worker agrees to the terms.
 The worker passes the hash they computed from the terms they read in the app.
 If it does not match what the farm stored, the transaction reverts — no silent
 bait-and-switch is possible. The Privy wallet call is the cryptographic signature.
 @param expectedHash  keccak256 the worker computed client-side

Farm cancels a mutually agreed engagement.
 The reason is stored on-chain — it is the only human-readable field we allow
 because it is dispute-relevant, not personally identifying.

KuluriAgreementFactory
 Neutral platform contract. Kuluri's backend deploys one of these once.
 The platform — not the farm, not the worker — controls who can register
 agreements through it. This is the key power-balance mechanism:
   - Only addresses the platform has whitelisted (verified farms) can call propose().
   - The factory's address is the `factory` immutable inside every KuluriAgreement,
     so fake "Kuluri" agreements deployed by other means are immediately detectable.
   - The factory is the single source of truth for the app to look up agreements.
 Anyone (worker, regulator, auditor) can query the factory to verify an agreement
 contract is genuine — without needing Kuluri's servers.

Whitelist a farm wallet so it can propose agreements directly (no backend relay).
 Revoke by passing allowed = false.

Verify that a contract address was created by this factory.
 A genuine Kuluri agreement will have factory() == address(this).
 Anyone can call this to check a contract is not a fake.
All agreement contracts a wallet is party to, newest first.
Contract address for an app-level agreement ID. Returns address(0) if unknown.

KuluriForwarder  —  EIP-2771 trusted meta-transaction forwarder
 How it works
 ────────────
 1. User's Privy wallet signs a ForwardRequest off-chain (free, no gas).
 2. Kuluri's backend submits execute() on-chain and pays the Gnosis Chain gas.
 3. This contract verifies the signature, then forwards the call to the target
    contract with the real user's address appended to the calldata (EIP-2771).
 4. KuluriAgreement reads the real sender from those last 20 bytes via _msgSender().
 Result: the user taps a button, their Privy wallet signs invisibly, the agreement
 is recorded on-chain under their address — they never hold xDAI or see gas fees.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks: each address has a counter that increments per call.

Verify that a signature is valid for a ForwardRequest.
 Call this off-chain before submitting to avoid wasting gas on bad signatures.

documentation.text:
Execute a signed ForwardRequest. Callable by anyone (the Kuluri backend relayer).
 Gas is paid by msg.sender (the relayer), not the user.
 The user's address is appended to the calldata so the target contract can read
 the true sender via _msgSender() (EIP-2771 convention).
